IEEE Software (Focus: Impact of AI on Productivity and Code), pp. 56-65. https://doi.org/10.1109/MS.2026.3678750. Date of publication 31 March 2026; current version 30 June 2026
Journal — IEEE Software (magazine), Focus section 'Impact of AI on Productivity and Code', DOI 10.1109/MS.2026.3678750

Çankaya University, Software Engineering Department, Ankara, Türkiye (Esirik; also Ph.D. candidate at Hacettepe University); Hacettepe University, Computer Engineering Department, Ankara, Türkiye (Gökalp)

Proposes an evaluation method; secondary: Compares — QAID (Quality Assessment for AI Development tools), a vendor-neutral multidimensional quality framework for AI coding assistants (6 dimensions, 17 subdimensions, 17 metrics, extending ISO/IEC 25010; expert weights by AHP and user weights by survey), built with design science research in five phases over 18 months; applied to compare four assistants (GPT-5.1, Gemini 3 Pro, Claude Sonnet 4.5, DeepSeek v3.2), largely from published benchmark and leaderboard scores

No SDD approach. Assistants evaluated: ChatGPT (GPT-5.1), Google Gemini (3 Pro), Claude (Sonnet 4.5), DeepSeek (v3.2; 'DeepSeek Coder (v3.2)' on p. 4); most recent versions available Nov-Dec 2025. Interface, agent or scaffold not stated

SUS-Efficiency (cost and energy efficiency) = max(0, 100 × (1 − Pmodel / Pbaseline)), Pmodel = average cost per 1M tokens (input + output), Pbaseline = US$15 industry ceiling (AA-Efficiency benchmark). OQ-Speed = (time to first token)^0.33 × (tokens per second)^0.33 × (total response time)^0.33 (AA-Speed)
Generation ability: GA-Genscore = Pass@1 × 100 (LiveCodeBench); GA-IRscore (SWE-bench leaderboard); GA-ACscore (Terminal-bench). All normalised to 0-100

Linguistic capability: LC-IFscore (IFBench), LC-Understanding (HLE, GPQA, MMLU-Pro, AIME), LC-CRscore context retention = (B/A) × 100 (AA-LCR). Operational quality: OQ-IDEmaturity (BARS). Interaction quality: IQ-SUSscore (SUS, Nielsen heuristics), IQ-Availability (BARS, pricing policies). Trustworthiness: TRS-Robust (Omniscience), TRS-Truth = (1 − Htotal/Ctotal) × 100 hallucination (Fortress), TRS-Secure (MASK), TRS-Safe (AIR-bench). Sustainability: SUS-Transparency (AA-Openness), SUS-Accountability (Stanford FMTI). Dimension scores = weighted sum of subdimensions; overall expert-weighted, user-weighted and equal-weighted scores

Mostly secondary data: benchmark/leaderboard scores retrieved from Artificialanalysis.ai, SWE-bench leaderboard, Scale leaderboard and HELM (Nov-Dec 2025), min-max normalised. Manual: expert assessments with structured rubrics (BARS) averaged across evaluators (Cronbach's α > 0.8); SUS/Nielsen heuristics by 15 UX experts; vendor websites and reports (pricing, governance). Weights: AHP pairwise comparisons by 15 experts (consistency ratio mean 0.06) and Likert survey (103 participants, α = 0.87)

Four assistants chosen for market prominence (>1M users), technical diversity and data availability; scored on the same 17 QAID metrics, mostly from public leaderboards (not run by the authors), Nov-Dec 2025, 'identical model versions' across platforms; three weighting schemes (expert, user, equal). No baseline. Agent/scaffold, operator and briefing not stated/N/A; acceptance tests only those inside the source benchmarks; repetitions not stated; no human-intervention rules. Robustness: Monte Carlo sensitivity (10,000 iterations, ±10% weights); cross-platform validation against Artificial Analysis intelligence index, LMArena web development and HELM safety (Spearman)

No tool dominates. Expert weighting: Claude 66.77 narrowly ahead of GPT 66.48; user weighting: GPT 64.86 leads (Claude 62.94); equal weighting: GPT 64.66, Claude 63.51; Gemini third (61.91-61.98), DeepSeek fourth (54.52-59.82). 'Significant differences (p < 0.05) between top-tier tools (GPT, Claude, Gemini) and DeepSeek across all dimensions' (test not named; no significance reported among GPT, Claude and Gemini). Gaps: trustworthiness 39.29 points (Claude 80.58 best), sustainability 52.77 (DeepSeek 86.46 best, Claude 33.69), operational quality 36.70, linguistic 9.75, generation 13.27 (Gemini best 67.62), interaction 3.80. Claude 1st in 94.2% of expert-weighted Monte Carlo scenarios, GPT 1st in 93.8% of user-weighted
fields.why: The significance claim is only between the three top-tier tools and DeepSeek (p. 6), not among all four tools as the draft implied; so the GPT vs Claude lead is not shown to be significant. Equal-weighted totals added.

fields.v: Distinguished the tools and showed ranking shifts by stakeholder weights; rankings stable under ±10% weight variation; convergent validity with external platforms on 3 dimensions (Spearman ρ = 0.90-1.00, n = 4 tools). Repeatability over reruns not tested. Limitations stated: reliance on published benchmark data and vendor-disclosed information, panel/survey size, temporal validity given rapid version updates

Limitations: reliance on published benchmark data and vendor-disclosed information; expert panel (n = 15) and survey (n = 103) may not represent all stakeholders; temporal limitations due to rapid version updates. Gaps/future work: longitudinal validation in real-world deployments, expanded tool coverage as standardised metrics emerge, automated evaluation pipelines, collaboration with regulators on transparent benchmarking standards. Earlier gaps from the authors' reviews: 89% of 127 studies focus on code completion accuracy, 76% use proprietary data sets, 68% a single language, 54% vendor-funded

Inconsistencies: Delphi panel stated as 15 experts but composition sums to 12 (5 + 4 + 3) (p. 4); Figure 1 numbers the phases differently from the text (e.g. survey and AHP/expert panel phases in another order; figure text is jumbled in the extraction) (p. 3-4); Table 4 ranking row (GPT 1st, Claude 2nd, Gemini 3rd, DeepSeek 4th) does not say which weighting it uses: it matches user and equal weighting but not the expert weighting, where the text says Claude leads (p. 6, 8); text says trustworthiness shows 'the largest variation' (39.29) while sustainability varies by 52.77 (p. 6), the conclusion names both as largest gaps (p. 10); metric prefix GF- in Figure 2 vs GA- in Tables 2-3; 'DeepSeek Coder (v3.2)' (p. 4) vs 'DeepSeek v3.2' elsewhere. Values used: Table 4 (p. 8). Statistical test for p < 0.05 not named; correlations on 4 tools; validation partly circular (QAID scores built from leaderboards validated against other leaderboards). No data or replication package (text claims 'publicly documented measurement criteria' but gives no link); no pre-registration. Programming language: Not stated
fields.why: The Table 4 ranking row is unlabelled and matches the user and equal weightings (GPT 64.86/64.66 > Claude 62.94/63.51), so it is not a plain contradiction; reworded as an unlabelled row that does not match the expert weighting. Figure 1 order is hard to read from the extracted text, so the claim is softened.

fields.why: Partly is a judgement: the main conclusions (no tool dominates, rankings shift with weights) do follow from Table 4; the problems are overclaims and inconsistencies rather than conclusions contradicting the data. A reader could give Yes or Partly. The ranking-row point was weakened (row matches user/equal weighting).
fields.doubt: As conclusões principais seguem da Tabela 4, mas há exageros (validação com 4 ferramentas, teste estatístico não nomeado, 'maior variação'). Decide entre Partly e Yes.
